lastText: ☰⚙File ClosedHeld to the Last Man, Lost to the LedgerImperial General Headquarters, Beginning 1939Imperial Headquarters chose a war against the Soviet Union over a war against the United States: withdrew from Siberia once the winter made the gamble's cost clear, ran that delayed operation deliberately, spending time it couldn't fully spare, starving the fleet's reserves to keep the Army's northern garrison intact. On balance, this was the harder road available to Tokyo in 1941. This staff declined to reckon with the cost in writing and pressed forward instead, the same unexamined momentum that let the original 1941 optimism go untested against Nomonhan's own lessons for as long as it did. The southern war fought two years late, on a ledger this command chose not to read, closes out anyway. The veteran air groups this timeline never bled out at Midway got their one real test against an American carrier force neither side had ever actually faced, a genuine unknown resolved rather than left standing, whatever the resolution actually cost.The Theater Map at the end of the warPacific Situation · The war as it ended · Theater MapJapan: ContestedFormosa: ContestedManchukuo: ContestedNorth China: ContestedEast China: ContestedGuangdong: ContestedHunan-Guangxi: Allied-controlled / liberatedFree China: Allied-controlled / liberatedYan'an: Allied-controlled / liberatedTibet & Xinjiang: Neutral / not yet contestedIndochina: ContestedThailand: ContestedBurma: Allied-controlled / liberated
